input.prompt: The camera itself is completely locked off and motionless like a tripod photograph, with absolutely no zoom, no push-in, no drift, no pan and no camera movement of any kind for the entire clip. The framed 'NO JAPANESE SAKE, NO LIFE.' pop-art poster on the wall (a hand holding a wooden masu cup on a pale grey background) stays perfectly rigid, flat and exactly the same size for the entire clip: its illustration, hand, masu cup, lettering, ALCOHOLIDAY logo, white border and proportions never warp, stretch, resize, shift position or change perspective, as if it truly is a static print and not a generated image. The only motion anywhere in this shot is the white hand towel with blue stripes hanging on the kitchen cabinet handle: it sways very gently back and forth as if touched by a soft breeze, and stays hanging on the handle. Everything else, including the window and the city outside, the chef jacket and the black apron on the hooks, the shelf, the boxes, the black bag, the low table with the notebook, pen, food container and cup, the cushion, the shoes and the poster, is completely still and motionless. A quiet, calm early evening at dusk in the small tidy one-room apartment of a 23-year-old who works at a Japanese restaurant, warm lamp light inside and a deep blue city sky outside. No steam, no smoke, no haze. No people. All motion is small, slow and calm.
